answer: In a logistics market serving an island, an oasis, and a canyon, each agent identity must lock a $100 bond before bidding, held until its deliveries settle. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up $100,000; new names do not create free bidding capacity. If an agent signs conflicting delivery receipts for the same shipment, anyone can submit both signatures to slash its bond, making that fraud costly even when the attacker abandons the identity.
